chunks.title: Approach to uveitis (SUN)
chunks.tldr: Describe: onset (sudden/insidious), duration (limited ≤3 mo / persistent), course (acute, recurrent >3 mo off Rx, chronic <3 mo off Rx), laterality, location (anterior: AC > vitreous; intermediate: vitreous > AC; posterior: retina/choroid; pan). White lesions = retina, yellow = choroid. Goals: infectious vs not, ocular vs systemic, exclude masquerade, test only if it changes management. Up to 40% undifferentiated.
points: Never call it anterior uveitis without looking at the retina.
Bloody hypopyon → herpes; shifting hypopyon → Behçet.
Controlled on drugs = 'suppressed', not 'in remission'.
CME or peripheral vasculitis alone don't make it posterior (pars planitis is intermediate).

cards.q: SUN definition of chronic uveitis?
cards.a: Persistent uveitis with relapse <3 months after stopping treatment.

chunks.title: Anterior uveitis: signs & causes
chunks.tldr: Pain, photophobia (consensual), flush, cells/flare. KP: fine diffuse → herpes, FHIC; coin-shaped → CMV; small NG → HLA-B27, JIA, drugs; mutton-fat → sarcoid, TB, syphilis, VKH, SO, lens. High IOP: herpes, PSS, FHIC, lens. Hypopyon/fibrin: B27, Behçet, endophthalmitis, rifabutin, tumour. Quiet eye: JIA, FHIC, masquerade. Causes: B27 (AS, reactive, psoriatic, IBD; alternating), herpes, JIA, FHIC, sarcoid, syphilis, TB, TINU, drugs (rifabutin, cidofovir, bisphosphonates, moxifloxacin, checkpoint inhibitors), UGH.
points: Iris atrophy: herpes (sectoral), oral moxifloxacin (BADI/BAIT).
TINU: young women, NSAID trigger, urinary β2-microglobulin.
Pigment cells (PDS) mimic — vanish with red-free light.
chunks.hook: Mutton-fat = granulomatous: Sarcoid, TB, Syphilis, VKH, SO.

cards.q: Bilateral alternating acute recurrent anterior uveitis suggests?
cards.a: HLA-B27-associated uveitis.

cards.q: Name two drugs that cause hypopyon uveitis.
cards.a: Rifabutin; also cidofovir, bisphosphonates, checkpoint inhibitors (rifabutin is classic).

chunks.title: Anterior uveitis: workup & treatment
chunks.tldr: No labs for first mild unilateral NG uveitis without systemic clues, known cause, or classic picture (herpes, FHIC, toxo). Otherwise targeted: bilateral/granulomatous/recurrent → syphilis serology, chest X-ray/CT (sarcoid), TB test if at risk; B27 if acute; AC tap PCR for herpes/toxo. Rx: prednisolone acetate 1% q1–6h (or difluprednate) + cycloplegic; sub-Tenon triamcinolone if severe unilateral; systemic steroid/IMT if bilateral severe. Taper slowly (1 drop/day every 3–7 days).
points: Glaucoma: aqueous suppressants; avoid pilocarpine; PGA OK if needed.
Herpes: oral antivirals long-term + low-dose steroid; CMV → valganciclovir.
JIA: young girls, pauciarticular, ANA+, silent, band keratopathy → regular screening, methotrexate/adalimumab; cataract surgery only after 3 months quiet.
FHIC: doesn't need steroids; cataract surgery does well (Amsler bleed).
TB uveitis: full 4-drug therapy even without lung disease.
Oral pred >60 mg → AVN risk; use IV methylpred; calcium/vit D.
chunks.hook: Steroid + cycloplegic now; taper slowly; test only what changes management.

cards.q: Typical JIA uveitis profile?
cards.a: Young girl, pauciarticular arthritis, ANA positive, RF negative, chronic silent bilateral anterior uveitis.

chunks.title: Intermediate uveitis & masquerades
chunks.tldr: Painless floaters, 15–40 yrs, bilateral. Snowballs (inferior vitreous), snowbank (pars planitis >70%), peripheral phlebitis, CME = main cause of vision loss. Causes: pars planitis, sarcoid, MS (MRI if neuro symptoms), Lyme, syphilis, TINU, toxocara, lymphoma (older). Rx: treat if CME/symptoms — sub-Tenon or intravitreal steroid/implants, oral pred, IMT/anti-TNF; cryo or laser to snowbank NV; PPV.
points: Masquerades: primary vitreoretinal lymphoma (>50, steroid-resistant, subretinal infiltrates → vitrectomy, IL-10, MYD88), RB, melanoma, RP, RRD, IOFB, leukaemia, amyloid, asteroid.
Cataract surgery: 3 months quiet; peri-op oral pred + NSAID/steroid drops.
Topical NSAIDs don't help uveitic CME; anti-VEGF only if uveitis suppressed.
chunks.hook: Old patient + vitritis that won't respond to steroids = lymphoma → biopsy.

cards.q: Most common cause of vision loss in pars planitis?
cards.a: Cystoid macular oedema.

chunks.title: White dot syndromes
chunks.tldr: APMPPE: young adults post-viral, bilateral creamy placoid lesions, block early, stain late; self-limiting — but cerebral vasculitis → MRA + steroids if headache. MEWDS: young woman, unilateral, tiny white dots, foveal granularity, wreath on FA, enlarged blind spot; recovers 6–8 weeks. Birdshot: middle-aged, cream ovals inferior/nasal, vitritis, HLA-A29 (~100%), ICG dark spots → early IMT. MCP: myopic women, histo-like spots with vitritis, CNV ⅓. PIC: myopic women, small spots, no inflammation, CNV up to 40%. Serpiginous: 30–60, spreading from disc, IMT; exclude TB serpiginous-like.
points: Toxocara: child, unilateral granuloma, macular drag.
POHS: no vitritis (vs MCP).
chunks.hook: Birdshot → A29. MEWDS → wreath, gets better by itself.

cards.q: HLA association of birdshot chorioretinopathy?
cards.a: HLA-A29.

cards.q: Systemic complication to consider in APMPPE with headache?
cards.a: Cerebral vasculitis (stroke risk) — image and give systemic steroids.

chunks.title: Retinitis & retinal vasculitis
chunks.tldr: CMV: immunocompromised, granular white necrosis + haemorrhage (pizza pie), little vitritis. ARN: peripheral necrosis, arteritis, marked vitritis, rapid. PORN: severe AIDS, posterior, no vitritis, spares vessels, very rapid. Toxo: headlight in fog next to old scar. Candida: fluffy white balls. Vasculitis: veins — sarcoid (candle-wax), syphilis, pars planitis, Eales, MS, birdshot; arteries — GCA, PAN, ARN, IRVAN, Susac; both — SLE, GPA, Behçet.
points: Cat scratch: neuroretinitis with macular star; Bartonella serology.
DUSN: nematode, unilateral, progressive → laser the worm.
Pain + posterior uveitis → think endophthalmitis or posterior scleritis.
chunks.hook: Lots of vitritis = ARN/toxo; almost none = CMV/PORN.

cards.q: Retinal vasculitis with candle-wax drippings?
cards.a: Sarcoidosis (periphlebitis).

chunks.title: HLA-B27 uveitis
chunks.tldr: Recurrent, unilateral or alternating, acute NG anterior uveitis, lots of fibrin, early synechiae; commonest cause of unilateral hypopyon; men. Associations: ankylosing spondylitis (morning back stiffness, SI joints), reactive arthritis (conjunctivitis + urethritis + arthritis), psoriatic, IBD. >½ have a spondyloarthropathy, often diagnosed only after the eye flare. Rx: intensive topical steroid + cycloplegic; IMT for frequent severe relapses.
points: Workup: HLA-B27, SI joint X-ray/CT, rheumatology; chlamydia swabs if reactive.
AS: cardiac review (aortic regurgitation, conduction).
chunks.hook: Young man, stiff back in the morning, fibrin in the AC = B27.

cards.q: Most common cause of unilateral hypopyon uveitis?
cards.a: HLA-B27-associated anterior uveitis.

chunks.title: Toxoplasmosis
chunks.tldr: Commonest posterior uveitis (~90% of focal necrotising retinitis). White retinitis next to an old pigmented scar + dense overlying vitritis = headlight in fog; Kyrieleis arteritis, ↑IOP. Peripheral small lesions in healthy people may be observed. Treat: macula, within 2–3 mm of disc, near big vessel, severe vitritis, or immunocompromised. Triple therapy 4–6 wk: pyrimethamine (load 200 mg then 25–50 mg) + folinic acid + sulfadiazine; prednisone after 24 h of antibiotics. Alternatives: TMP-SMX, clindamycin, azithromycin, atovaquone, intravitreal clindamycin.
points: No periocular steroids.
Weekly CBC on pyrimethamine; no folic acid vitamins.
Pregnancy: no pyrimethamine → spiramycin.
Immunocompromised: little vitritis, multifocal/bilateral, no scar → CNS imaging; maintenance TMP-SMX.
Negative IgG makes toxo unlikely; aqueous PCR more specific.
Peri-op TMP-SMX prophylaxis for cataract surgery in prior toxo.
chunks.hook: Headlight in the fog beside an old scar = toxo. No depot steroid!

cards.q: Why is folinic acid given with pyrimethamine?
cards.a: To reduce bone-marrow suppression (pyrimethamine is a folate antagonist).

cards.q: Name four indications to treat ocular toxoplasmosis.
cards.a: Macular lesion, within 2–3 mm of disc, threatening a major vessel, severe vitritis reducing vision (or immunocompromised).

chunks.title: Sarcoidosis
chunks.tldr: 20–50 yrs, African Americans & Scandinavians. Mutton-fat KP, iris nodules (Koeppe/Busacca), extensive synechiae, conjunctival nodules, lacrimal enlargement, intermediate uveitis, candle-wax periphlebitis, choroidal granulomas, disc granuloma. Systemic: hilar nodes, erythema nodosum, lupus pernio, VII palsy, parotids. Tests: chest CT (> CXR), ACE (60–90%), lysozyme (kids), biopsy non-caseating granuloma (skin/node — not erythema nodosum), gallium (panda/lambda).
points: Rx: anterior → topical; posterior → periocular/oral steroid; topical alone inadequate for posterior disease; methotrexate, MMF, infliximab.
ACE falsely low on steroids/ACE inhibitors; raised in TB, HIV, histo.
Blind conjunctival biopsy without visible nodule: low yield.

cards.q: Gallium scan 'panda' and 'lambda' signs indicate?
cards.a: Panda: lacrimal/parotid uptake; lambda: bilateral hilar + right paratracheal nodes — suggestive of sarcoidosis.

chunks.title: Behçet disease
chunks.tldr: 20–40 yrs, Silk Road (Turkish, Middle Eastern, Japanese). Recurrent painful oral ulcers (≥3/yr) + 2 of: genital ulcers, skin lesions (erythema nodosum, pseudofolliculitis), pathergy, eye disease. Eye: bilateral shifting hypopyon (no fibrin), occlusive vasculitis of arteries and veins, necrotising retinitis, optic atrophy. HLA-B51. Blind in 3–4 years untreated. Rx: steroids + early anti-TNF (infliximab/adalimumab) first-line; rule out TB, syphilis, hepatitis first.
points: Neuro-Behçet, pulmonary artery aneurysm, bowel ulcers.
DDx: B27 (fibrin, unilateral), ARN, sarcoid, syphilis, SLE, GPA.
chunks.hook: Mouth ulcers + shifting hypopyon + occluded vessels = Behçet → anti-TNF.

cards.q: Why does the Behçet hypopyon shift with head position?
cards.a: There is little fibrin, so the cells stay mobile (unlike HLA-B27).

chunks.title: Acute retinal necrosis
chunks.tldr: Usually immunocompetent. Peripheral confluent necrosis, circumferential spread, occlusive arteritis, marked vitritis, pain; macula spared early. VZV (older), HSV (younger). RRD in ~70%; fellow eye in ⅓ (usually within 6 weeks). Aqueous PCR. Rx: oral valacyclovir 1–2 g tds (or famciclovir; IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg tds alternative) + intravitreal foscarnet/ganciclovir; ≥2–3 months (some lifelong); steroid after 24 h; ± barrier laser; PPV + oil for RD.
points: PORN: severe AIDS, deep multifocal, posterior early, no vitritis, spares vessels — rapid bilateral blindness.
Treatment protects the fellow eye; doesn't reduce RD in the first eye.
chunks.hook: ARN: Antivirals now, Retina will detach, Neighbour eye at risk.

cards.q: Rate of retinal detachment after ARN?
cards.a: About 70%.

chunks.title: CMV retinitis & HIV retinopathy
chunks.tldr: CD4 <100 (screen every 3–6 months), transplant, chemo, even after intravitreal steroid. Granular brushfire border, ± haemorrhage (pizza pie), mild vitritis, stellate KP. RRD in ⅓. Rx: valganciclovir 900 mg bd × 21 d → 900 mg daily (or IV ganciclovir/foscarnet) ± intravitreal for macula-threatening; start/optimise HAART. Stop maintenance if CD4 >100 for >6 months and quiet. Immune recovery uveitis (vitritis, CME, ERM) after reconstitution → steroids. HIV microvasculopathy: CWS, haemorrhages, MAs in 50–70%; no Rx.
points: Ganciclovir/valganciclovir: marrow toxicity; foscarnet: renal, electrolytes, seizures; cidofovir: nephrotoxic, hypotony, uveitis (give probenecid; never intravitreal).
Resistance: UL97, UL54 mutations.
Systemic therapy cuts mortality and fellow-eye disease vs intravitreal alone.
chunks.hook: CD4 under 100 + brushfire retina = CMV → valganciclovir + HAART.

cards.q: When can CMV maintenance therapy be stopped?
cards.a: CD4 >100 cells/mm³ for >6 months on HAART with quiescent retinitis.

chunks.title: Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada
chunks.tldr: Autoimmune attack on melanocytes; women 20–50 with pigmented skin (Asian, Hispanic, Middle Eastern, Native American). No trauma/surgery. Bilateral granulomatous panuveitis with multiple serous RDs, thick choroid, disc swelling; FA pinpoint leaks ('starry sky'). Phases: prodrome (headache, meningism, tinnitus, hearing loss, scalp sensitivity, CSF pleocytosis) → uveitic → convalescent (vitiligo, poliosis, alopecia, sunset-glow fundus) → chronic recurrent. Rx: high-dose oral/IV steroids, taper very slowly, early steroid-sparing IMT.
points: Complete = eye + neuro/auditory + skin; incomplete = eye + one; probable = eye only (Harada).
DDx serous RD: SO (trauma history), posterior scleritis (T-sign, unilateral), malignant HTN, preeclampsia, CSCR, uveal effusion, APMPPE, tumours.
Recurrence up to 9 months after stopping steroids.
chunks.hook: Headache + ringing ears + bilateral serous RDs = VKH.

cards.q: Convalescent fundus appearance in VKH?
cards.a: Sunset-glow fundus (diffuse depigmentation), ± Dalen–Fuchs-like scars.

chunks.title: Ocular syphilis
chunks.tldr: The great imitator: any uveitis (posterior/pan commonest), optic neuritis, IK, scleritis, retinitis. Pathognomonic-ish: acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis, punctate inner retinitis, iris roseola. Test: treponemal first (EIA/CIA, FTA-ABS), then RPR/VDRL titre for activity. HIV test everyone. Ocular syphilis = neurosyphilis: LP, then IV aqueous penicillin G 3–4 MU q4h × 10–14 days (± benzathine 2.4 MU weekly × 3). Oral steroids after 24–48 h (Jarisch–Herxheimer).
points: Treponemal + / RPR − with no documented treatment → still treat.
Follow RPR 3-monthly: should fall 4× in 6 months.
Penicillin allergy → desensitise (or ceftriaxone 2 g daily × 10–14 d).
HIV co-infection may give negative serology.
Congenital: Hutchinson triad (IK, notched teeth, deafness), salt-and-pepper fundus.
chunks.hook: Any weird uveitis → test syphilis. Eye syphilis is brain syphilis → IV penicillin.

cards.q: Treatment of syphilitic uveitis?
cards.a: Neurosyphilis regimen: IV aqueous crystalline penicillin G 3–4 million units q4h for 10–14 days.

cards.q: What is the 'reverse algorithm' for syphilis testing?
cards.a: Treponemal test first (EIA/CIA); if positive, quantitative nontreponemal (RPR/VDRL) to gauge activity.

chunks.title: Acute postoperative endophthalmitis
chunks.tldr: Days after surgery: pain + ↓vision + hypopyon/fibrin + vitritis. Organisms: S. epidermidis commonest; S. aureus, strep (strep after injections/blebs), Gram-negatives. Tap and inject now: vancomycin 1 mg + ceftazidime 2.25 mg (amikacin if allergic) ± dexamethasone. EVS: immediate PPV if LP vision (post-cataract); HM or better → tap/inject. Review q12–24h; pain relief = early response; re-inject at 48 h if worse.
points: Prevention: 5% povidone-iodine; intracameral antibiotics.
TASS: 6–24 h, diffuse corneal oedema, sterile → intensive steroids.
Other mimics: sterile post-triamcinolone, B27 flare, retained lens.
Look for wound leak, exposed suture, vitreous wick, blepharitis.
B-scan if no view.
chunks.hook: EVS: LP → vitrectomy; HM or better → tap & inject.

cards.q: EVS indication for immediate vitrectomy?
cards.a: Presenting vision of light perception only (post-cataract endophthalmitis).

cards.q: How does TASS differ from infectious endophthalmitis?
cards.a: Onset 6–24 h, diffuse limbus-to-limbus corneal oedema, little pain/vitritis, sterile — responds to steroids.

chunks.title: Chronic post-op uveitis & C. acnes
chunks.tldr: Normal post-op inflammation settles by 6 weeks. Persisting: poor compliance/fast taper, retained lens, vitreous/iris in wound, UGH, RD, epithelial downgrowth (white spots after argon), pre-existing uveitis, SO. Subacute endophthalmitis: Cutibacterium acnes — weeks–months, granulomatous KP, small hypopyon, white capsular plaque, transient steroid response; anaerobic culture held 14 days. Rx: intravitreal vancomycin, PPV + partial capsulectomy → if fails, remove IOL + capsule. Fungi → intravitreal amphotericin/voriconazole.
points: Gonio + UBM for retained fragments and IOL position.
chunks.hook: White plaque in the bag + smouldering uveitis = C. acnes.

cards.q: How long should cultures be held for suspected C. acnes?
cards.a: 14 days, anaerobic.

chunks.title: Traumatic & endogenous endophthalmitis
chunks.tldr: Traumatic: exclude IOFB (thin-cut CT); Bacillus = fulminant, fever, ring ulcer. Rx: repair, remove IOFB, intravitreal vanc + ceftazidime ± clindamycin, systemic FQ (moxifloxacin) + cefazolin, tetanus; hold steroids until fungi excluded. Endogenous bacterial: septic, lines, IVDU, endocarditis, liver abscess (Klebsiella in East Asia), B. cereus in IVDU; may be bilateral. Admit, cultures, echo, IV antibiotics ≥2 weeks, ± intravitreal and PPV.
points: Organic matter injury → fungal risk.
IVDU: add aminoglycoside + clindamycin (Bacillus).
Intravitreal aminoglycosides can infarct the macula.
chunks.hook: Trauma + fever + ring ulcer + rapid loss = Bacillus.

cards.q: Typical cause of endogenous endophthalmitis in East Asia?
cards.a: Klebsiella pneumoniae (from liver abscess).

chunks.title: Candida endophthalmitis
chunks.tldr: Lines, TPN, recent abdominal surgery, immunosuppression, IVDU. Fluffy yellow-white chorioretinal lesions → break into vitreous as 'string of pearls'/cotton balls. Screen all candidaemia within 72 h, repeat at 2 weeks. Chorioretinitis only → systemic fluconazole (800 mg load, 400–800 daily) or voriconazole/liposomal amphotericin for resistant. Vitreous involvement → intravitreal amphotericin 5–10 µg or voriconazole 50–100 µg ± PPV.
points: Monitor LFTs on azoles; renal function/electrolytes on amphotericin.
Pneumocystis choroidopathy: yellow round choroidal lesions, no vitritis, AIDS on pentamidine.

cards.q: Classic vitreous appearance in Candida endophthalmitis?
cards.a: Fluffy 'cotton balls' / 'string of pearls'.

chunks.title: Sympathetic ophthalmia
chunks.tldr: Bilateral granulomatous panuveitis after penetrating trauma or surgery (now mostly repeated vitreoretinal surgery) to one eye; usually 4–8 weeks later, 90% within 1 year. Mutton-fat KP, Dalen–Fuchs nodules, thick choroid, serous RD, papillitis; earliest sign may be loss of accommodation in the good eye. Rx: high-dose oral steroid → long-term IMT or steroid implants. Enucleation within 14 days only for a truly unsalvageable eye; no benefit once SO starts.
points: DDx: VKH (no trauma), phacoantigenic (one eye), sarcoid, syphilis, TB.
With treatment, ~81% keep ≥20/40.
chunks.hook: Injured one eye, now both inflamed = sympathetic ophthalmia.

cards.q: Histological hallmark of sympathetic ophthalmia?
cards.a: Dalen–Fuchs nodules (and diffuse granulomatous choroiditis sparing the choriocapillaris).
